page_map_registration.status: native macOS/ASan/kernel/KC passed on 358e6c1; device visibility unverified
page_map_registration.defect: override/src/linux_page.c:vmmap_add wrote vm_size/vm_addr/vm_handle through kmalloc(sizeof(*vmmap), GFP_KERNEL) without checking it, and returned void, so a refused registration both dereferenced NULL and left the caller unable to unwind the device or IOKit mapping it had already created.
page_map_registration.repair: vmmap_add returns -ENOMEM; _ioremap_attr rolls back with pmap_unmapdev(addr, size) and vmap/linuxkpi_vmap_pfn with nmx_xnu_unmap(handle). The generated override/src/linux_page.c and the fork script that regenerates it both carry the change, and it reaches the build only through patches/xkpi.patch.
page_map_registration.executed: actual vmmap_add/vmmap_remove, is_vmalloc_addr, _ioremap_attr, iounmap, vmap, linuxkpi_vmap_pfn and vunmap, joined to the actual pmap_mapdev_attr/pmap_unmapdev device registry
covered: device mapping registered by address; iounmap releases the device record and the IOKit handle exactly once
vmap and linuxkpi_vmap_pfn register the IOKit handle; vunmap releases it exactly once
refused vmmap registration returns NULL and gives back exactly what was created (pmap_unmapdev for the device path, nmx_xnu_unmap for the vmap paths)
a refused staging array maps nothing, releases nothing and leaves nothing allocated
a refused native mapping leaves no device record, no vmmap record and nothing to release
the registry stays usable after a refusal
iounmap/vunmap of an unknown address release nothing
